question: What was the fraction of sales price collected as tax under the Mauryans?
solution:
The correct answer is __**(1)/(10)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Under the Mauryan Empire, a fraction of the sales price collected as tax was **(1)/(10)**.
 
• This tax was known as **"Bhaga,"** which means a share or portion.
 
• The Mauryan administration was known for its **efficient revenue collection system**.
 
• Taxation was a primary source of revenue for the Mauryan state to maintain its large army and administrative machinery.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Arthashastra:**

 
 
• The Arthashastra, written by Kautilya (Chanakya), was a treatise on statecraft, economic policy, and military strategy during the Mauryan period.
 
• It provides detailed insights into the Mauryan taxation system, including the collection of taxes and duties.
 
 
 
• **Revenue Sources:**
 
 
• Other significant sources of revenue included taxes on land (Bhaga), tolls, customs duties, and fines.
 
• Land tax, which was usually one-sixth of the produce, was a major contributor to the state’s revenue.
 
 
 
• **Administration:**
 
 
• The Mauryan administration was highly centralized, with the king at the top, followed by ministers and other officials.
 
• Revenue officers, known as Samaharta, were responsible for the collection of taxes.
 
 
 
• **Infrastructure Development:**
 
 
• The revenue collected was used for infrastructure development, including the construction of roads, irrigation systems, and public buildings.
 
• The state also maintained granaries and warehouses to ensure food security.
